## BOOK 1 of 3: THE WORLD MASTERS, by George Griffith (Gutenberg 38028; publisher John Long, London 1903)
Front matter: "Ready shortly"; other works by author: Sidelights on Convict Life; titles listed: The Angel of the Revolution, Brothers of the Chain, The Justice of Revenge, A Honeymoon in Space, Captain Johnnie. Publisher John Long, 13 and 14 Norris Street, Haymarket.

**PROLOGUE "The Moment of Triumph":** Strassburg, night, old Fisher's Gate, River Ill, citadel. Dr Emil Fargeau (~60, tall, stooping, iron-grey hair, Alsatian patois, professor of physical science at Strassburg). Laboratory in attic: machine ~3 ft high, glass cylinder, four glass supports, piece of steel ~4 in square, 1 in thick, under ring of needles; humming; ancient wooden clock with cuckoo. He strikes steel with wooden mallet; it shatters. Speech: will break Germany; France to be mistress/queen of world; "Soul of the World, Living Principle of Material Things"; metals useless to those who don't pay tribute; daughter Adelaide (of Bourbon line) to wed his son Victor, to restore throne of Saint Louis, Prince of Condé. He has ten twenty-mark pieces (~£10); owes Jew Weinthal (Judenstrasse) for a draft, forged figures; "a month to run".

**CHAPTER I:** 27 January (Kaiser's birthday), German Embassy, Nevski Prospekt, St Petersburg. Prince Louis Xavier de Condé, Duc de Montpensier (~50, Bourbon features, Order of St Vladimir, Golden Fleece, royalist, refuses French orders) and daughter Adelaide de Condé, Marquise de Montpensier (not yet 21). Captain Victor Fargeau, Uhlan, military attaché (~28, blue eyes). Countess Sophie Valdemar (19, golden-bronze hair, pansy-blue eyes, sensual mouth), daughter of Count Leo Valdemar, Chief of Third Section; Count Valdemar (big, bearded). Sophie hates Adelaide; overhears Victor tell Adelaide "he had succeeded... goes to Paris." French Ambassador absent (conference with Count Lansdorf and Little Father).

**CHAPTER II:** Emil Fargeau pleads with French Minister of War (incredulous; demands demonstration; references magnetic tides, Faraday; mentions Gulf Stream diversion scheme). Refused; minister offers 50-franc note; "Pfennige" sneer. Fargeau's broken speech: "Tant pis pour toi". Fargeau, with a hundred francs left, writes letters: to Victor (Petersburg), to Reuss Weinthal (Judenstrasse, Strassburg), and a tin-cased specification. Straps coat-pocket packet to his back, takes Nord Station train to Southampton via Le Havre; at midnight jumps from steamer; screw mangles him; tin box lashed to body.

**CHAPTER III:** May morning, steam yacht *Nadine*, between Guernsey and Southampton. Ernest Shafto Hardress, Viscount Branston (heir of Earl of Orrel), with Frank Lamson, M.A., D.Sc. (32, gold medal). Body spotted; tin box cut free. Lady Olive (Hardress's sister, ~25, Irish eyes). Miss Chrysie Vandel (daughter of Clifford K. Vandel, President of American Electrical Storage Trust, Buffalo, NY). Chrysie quotes Kipling "Inopportune, shrill-accented" lines. Mr Jackson orders body sewn in canvas.

**CHAPTER IV:** Lamson opens box alone, reads; locks door; temptation; tells Hardress "How would you like to be master of the world?" Papers hidden in hip-pocket. Lamson's scheme: magnetic/electric storage; "electrolise" ships. Hardress willing to syndicate.

**CHAPTER V:** Orrel Court (Hampshire, South Downs). Dinner: Earl Harry Shafto Hardress, eighth Earl of Orrel; Vandel ("Lightning King"); Vandel's late wife American. Name "International Magnetic Control Syndicate." Lamson explains scheme. Vandel vows to make big money; resolution "masters of the world."

**CHAPTER VI:** Trip plans: Vandel president; Lamson to study US machinery; Hardress to lease Boothia Felix (Magnetic Pole) from Canadian govt, £1000/yr for 10 years. Hardress proposes to Chrysie at Buffalo; she gives conditional answer ("option on territory"). Vandel accepts. Prince de Condé and Adelaide travel to Elsenau.

**CHAPTER VII:** Hôtel Wilhelmshof, Elsenau (spa, Thuringia/Hartz). Lord Orrel and Lady Olive; prince & Adelaide arrive; Adelaide and Olive friendly. Orrel and prince: friends since Aix-les-Bains; Orrel's brother died fighting for France 1870. Prince voices anti-democratic views, hints at Fargeau's discovery.

**CHAPTER VIII:** Orrel tells prince the Nadine story; prince collapses in rage/grief ("Mon Dieu... it is the same!"). Prince's madness that night; Adelaide locks door; prince dies of broken brain vessel, last words "France! O ma belle France... et moi ton roi." Hardress arrives from Paris that evening.

**CHAPTER IX:** Funeral in Elsenau pines, brick grave. Adelaide's diary entries: loves Hardress; plans to tell Victor little; Sophie's ally. Diary line: "I wonder if there is another woman?"

**CHAPTER X:** Madame de Condé (Princess of Bourbon) at Vienna Ringstrasse hotel. Orrel/Hardress: Hardress loves Chrysie. Adelaide & Victor in Vienna: Victor resolves to go to Paris, resign commission; Adelaide tells him Hardress syndicate is building storage works; he plans to offer "duplicate" papers to France.

**CHAPTER XI:** Victor in Paris; friend Gaston Leraulx (Ministry of War secretary); General Ducros (Minister of War). Adelaide visits with Victor. Sophie & Count Valdemar call; Sophie notes Boothia; Victor lies.

**CHAPTER XII:** Russian trapper & French-Canadian voyageur telegrams reach Ducros/Petersburg. Valdemars dine with Ducros: plan to share Polar expedition; Ducros allows use of his private room for overhearing. Victor offers scheme: French Arctic expedition with old warships and guns; Ducros agrees; Russia to share.

**CHAPTER XIII:** One year later, Cowes week, Orrel Court. Chrysie suspects Adelaide; Vandel says "Polar expeditions" are really for Boothia; cable to Lamson.

**CHAPTER XIV:** Sophie plots with father: kidnapping Nadine via Russian yacht Vlodoya; engineer Edward Williams (second engineer, seduced by Sophie, disgruntled inventor). Lamson cable from Vandel.

**CHAPTER XV:** Storage Works at Port Adelaide, Boothia Land; Lamson, Austin Vandel (nephew). Telegraph to Winnipeg. Tower over magnetic pole; absorber; steel masts 300 ft. Decision to bring Anglo-American party to Port Adelaide. Lamson & Austin.

**CHAPTER XVI:** Adelaide learns of Russia's ice-breaker *Ivan the Terrible*. Adelaide/Sophie spar; Chrysie vs Adelaide. Hardress tells of German spy scandal (Fargeau's extradition demanded). Count Valdemar plans with Sophie.

**CHAPTER XVII:** Sophie proposes drugging *Nadine*; Adelaide refuses then yields, swearing to protect Hardress/family. Chrysie observes. Telegram intercept: *Nadine* leaving early; Sophie gets Adelaide's complicity.

**CHAPTER XVIII:** Cowes week over; Nadine departs at night; Edward Williams sabotages engine (sanding/gritting shaft). Chrysie's telegram copy; "Dépêchez." Vandel's Vandelite gun. Guns mounted on Nadine.

**CHAPTER XIX:** Full speed; Williams detected; Vandel's arguments; Nadine 20 knots.

**CHAPTER XX:** Morning: guns mounted; Chrysie's revolver; drugged punch "à le Grand Monarque" by Adelaide; Captain Burgess, chief engineer M'Niven; Vlodoya approaches; Vandel's gun repels.

**CHAPTER XXI–XXIII:** Drugged crew; Vlodoya sunk; Count and Sophie captured; Chrysie fires Maxim; Nadine goes on to Boothia Land; Vlodoya's cargo stripped, boats set adrift.

**CHAPTER XXIV–XXV:** Press storm; France/Germany crisis; Trust circular ("capitation fee... one dollar per head per week"); six armed vessels; Rhine/European war; Storage works turned on; mass-scale electrical paralysis; guns burst (Charles Martel etc.); Europe paralysed.

**CHAPTER XXVI–XXVII:** Kaiser and President Loubet at Claridge's; King Edward mediates. Russian and French expedition arrive at Port Adelaide.

**CHAPTER XXVIII–XXIX:** Dinner at works; Admirals Nazanoff (Russian) and Dumont (French), Victor Fargeau, Professor Karnina. Ultimatum; Sophie sings Russian hymn; Adelaide shoots Hardress; Chrysie wounded; Lamson's death-ray disintegrates Sophie, Adelaide, Victor.

**CHAPTER XXX–XXXI:** Count Valdemar killed at gun; battle; expeditions destroyed; Caiman, Ivan survive. Madame de Bourbon sent home; boxes of ashes.

**EPILOGUE:** Hardress and Chrysie's engagement; Lamson; "The Powers have surrendered at discretion"; arbitration rules; "we four... run the world." Final lines: "And they kissed." (Printer's catalogue of Long's books follows.)

Key names: Fargeau (Emil, Victor), Adelaide de Condé, Prince Louis Xavier, Sophie & Count Leo Valdemar, Hardress, Lamson, Chrysie & Clifford Vandel, Lady Olive, Lord Orrel, Austin Vandel, Ducros, Leraulx, Edward Williams, Captain Burgess, M'Niven, Weinthal, King Edward, Kaiser, Loubet.

## BOOK 2 of 3: MORLEY ASHTON: A Story of the Sea, by James Grant (Gutenberg 64080–64082; Tinsley Brothers, London 1876; three volumes, merged)
**VOL I** (chapters I–XXVII)
- I "The Blind Goddess": Morley Ashton returns to Acton-Rennel (Norman cross, Cherrywood Hill, Acton Chine, Acton Chase, Shamble-oak). Engaged to Ethel Basset (~20). Split sixpence token; her lock of hair. Ethel's father Mr Scriven Basset (ex-barrister, Laurel Lodge), sister Rose (~18). Morley was 3 yrs agent on Bonny River (West Africa, Liverpool house); friend Tom Bartelot of brig *Rattler*. Basset appointed judge of Isle of France (Mauritius).
- II "Laurel Lodge": Morley's background (father merchant, failed). Captain Cramply Hawkshaw, son of Tom Hawkshaw of Lincoln's Inn, self-styled Texan "Partizan Rangers" captain, sinister, rival for Ethel; wears scarlet tarboosh/Spanish sash; gives Ethel a green-stone ring.
- III "Cramply Hawkshaw": Rose's introduction. Hawkshaw's lasso tales. Ethel's song-verse poem.
- IV "Rivalry": Hawkshaw's Barranca Secca tale: brothers Zuares and Pedro Barradas; Zuares kills his mother (Hawkshaw tells it).
- V "Suspicion": Morley wants passage; Ethel gives ring to Morley to return to Hawkshaw.
- VI "For the Last Time": Morley gets passage on *Hermione*. Hawkshaw intercepts telegram/letter. Church farewell.
- VII "The Rejection": Hawkshaw proposes to Ethel at Acton Chase; she refuses.
- VIII "Morley and Hawkshaw": at Acton Chine; Hawkshaw ostensibly drinks; Morley returns ring.
- IX "Alarm": Hawkshaw returns alone; search; hat & glove found at the Chine.
- X "Poor Ethel": Ethel's grief; Hawkshaw comforts. Morley's room; Ethel's wish to be buried.
- XI "Darkness made Light": Hawkshaw pushes Morley over Acton Chine; "Save me, Ethel!"
- XII "On board the good ship *Hermione*, of London": Captain John Phillips, Mr Quail (mate), Mr Foster, Manfredi (3rd mate, Italian, brother Attilio story), Dr Leslie Heriot (Scot, FRCSE), Nance Folgate (nurse), Joe steward. Pedro Barradas on yard. Hawkshaw passenger.
- XIII "Acton Chine": Morley on ledge 40 ft down; rescued by *Princess* (Tom Bartelot, Bill Morrison, Noah Gawthrop).
- XIV "The Rescue": rescued by *Princess*; Morrison (Scot mate).
- XV "An Old Shipmate": Bartelot reveals ship *Princess* bound Rio.
- XVI "Under the Tropic of Capricorn": voyage.
- XVII "Second Hearing": Morrison's tales (second-sight; cursed boat of Magnus Sigurdson).
- XVIII "Rio de Janeiro": Morley seeks passage to Mauritius; letter posted.
- XIX "Ethel amid the Atlantic Isles": Hermione at Teneriffe/Lanzarote; Pedro recognises Hawkshaw; Zuares kills shark.
- XX "Moonlight on the Sea": Manfredi's Attilio story (Austrian shooting at Pistoja, 1850; Colonel Count Rudolf de Veinrich).
- XXI "The Story of a Brave Boy": Attilio shot.
- XXII "Zuares and the Shark": Zuares fights shark.
- XXIII "Hawkshaw's Old Friends": Pedro threatens Hawkshaw; a corpse (Morley's face seen) is sunk.
- XXIV "Up Anchor": Morley in Rio; *Princess* sails for Tasmania; Tristan d'Acunha.
- XXV "The Suspicious Sail": brigantine chase; Scotch skipper's bottle tale.
- XXVI "The Strange Island": uninhabited island; hermit's hut.
- XXVII "The Hermit": dying old hermit, Don Pedro Zuares Miguel de Barradas (Knight of Santiago), inscription; buried; written confession.

**VOL II** (chapters I–XXV)
- I "Mariquita Escudero": Barradas hermit's confession (Mariquita, daughter of Miguel Escudero of Orizaba; seduced; Juan killed in duel; Pedro & Zuares sons; hermit shipwrecked). Hermit's confession is read by Morrison.
- II "The Crew of the Hermione Discontented": Hawkshaw's disquiet; Sharkey confrontation with Manfredi (marlinespike).
- III "Rose and Dr. Heriot": Heriot proposes to Rose; ring.
- IV "Man Overboard": Manfredi lost overboard.
- V "The Livid Face": ghostly face at porthole; Ethel & Rose's cabin.
- VI "What the Doctor Overheard in the Forecastle Bunks": mutiny plot (Barradas, Badger, Sharkey, Bolter, Quaco).
- VII "Measures for Defence Concerted": barricade, pistols.
- VIII "The Sail to Windward": *Princess* keeps course; storm.
- IX "The Storm": *Princess* wrecked, mates lost.
- X "The Four Castaways": Morley, Bartelot, Morrison, Gawthrop on raft; Prussian barque *Einicheit* refuses.
- XI "Captain Hawkshaw makes a Discovery to Leeward": *Hermione* rescues castaways; Hawkshaw sees Morley.
- XII "Dr Heriot's Patients": castaways aboard.
- XIII "Captain Hawkshaw's Troubles Increase": Hawkshaw resolves to kill Morley.
- XIV "Hawkshaw turns Nurse": plan to strangle.
- XV "A Biter Bitten": Morley's hand bitten by Noah.
- XVI "Dread": Hawkshaw claims a madman bit him.
- XVII "Unmasked": Morley reveals Hawkshaw's crime.
- XVIII "The Expulsion": Hawkshaw put in Coventry.
- XIX "The Meeting": Morley and Ethel reunited.
- XX "The Corpse-Licht": Morrison's tale of Hester Udny & Willie's skeleton.
- XXI "Out of Scylla and into Charybdis": Hawkshaw plans with Pedro.
- XXII "Four Bells in the Dog-watch": crew's mutiny meeting; Hawkshaw joins.
- XXIII "The Crisis at Last": Badger and Morrison; mutiny begins.
- XXIV "How the Ship Broached To": mutiny; Quail killed.
- XXV "The Cabin Attacked": carronade fired into cabin; Mr Basset hanged by mutineers at foreyard (via Badger, Pedro, Zuares) and saved by Heriot.

**VOL III** (chapters I–XXIV, plus Epilogue)
- I "Sail Ho!": ship rescued briefly by H.M.S. *Clyde*.
- II "The Fortitude of Ethel": family in cabin.
- III "The Door in the Bulkhead": Pedro kidnaps Ethel through bulkhead door.
- IV "Ethel among the Mutineers": Hawkshaw rescues Ethel; killed by mutineers.
- V "A Snare Laid": Pedro's arm shattered (Hawkshaw's shot).
- VI "Mr. Basset Deluded": Mr Basset hanged/killed.
- VII "Lux Venit ab Alto": Heriot resuscitates Mr Basset.
- VIII "The Valley of the Shadow": Mr Basset survives.
- IX "The Quarter-boat and its Freight": mutineers set adrift.
- X "Pedro's Wound": Pedro's arm amputated.
- XI "Remorse": Pedro's confession; Hermit's sons; mother Mariquita.
- XII "Story of a Modern Spanish Rogue": Pedro's Valparaiso adventures (alias Don Pedro Florez de Serrano).
- XIII "Ignez de Moreno": Pedro saves Ignez from drowning.
- XIV "How Pedro provided Himself with a Horse and Valet": Hawkshaw's horse stolen; Zuares as valet.
- XV "The Alameda de la Canada": Pedro's visit to Morenos in Santiago.
- XVI "The Dressing-closet of Ignez": Pedro hides in closet; Perez drags him out.
- XVII "The Great Crime of Pedro Barradas": church fire (Iglesia de la Compañía, 8 Dec, ~2,000 dead).
- XVIII "Committed to the Deep": Pedro dies; buried.
- XIX "Dr Heriot's Fee": Heriot marries Rose; Ethel & Morley engaged.
- XX "Radama Puffadder": Malay boatman; Mangrove Creek, Madagascar.
- XXI "The Mangrove Creek": three red proas attack.
- XXII "Eight Against Eighty": defence with carronades.
- XXIII "We'll go to Sea no more": Scots ship *Duke of Rothesay* (Captain Duncan Davidson) rescues.
- XXIV "The Anchor is let go": Port Louis, Mauritius; Morley & Ethel inherit £3000/yr each; Basset resigns; Heriot & Rose sail to Singapore on *Hermione* with Morrison.
- XXV "Conclusion": Eight months later at Laurel Lodge, Ethel and Morley married; Rose & Heriot married; Heriot practice at Acton-Rennel. Ends "THE END."

## BOOK 3 of 3: THE ROMANCE OF GOLDEN STAR, by George Griffith (Gutenberg 20173; F.V. White, 1897; illustrations by Alfred Pearse)
Epigraph: prophecy of Vilcaroya-Inca and Golden Star, "Son of the Sacred Race" with "pure virgin of his own holy blood" passing "through the Gate of Death" to cast down oppressor and raise Rainbow Banner on Golden Throne of Incas.

**PROLOGUE I "His Highness the Mummy":** Professor Martin Lamson (archaeologist, South American antiquities) with friend Dr Laurens Djama (physiologist, ~32, Kilburn/Brondesbury Park, previously saved Lamson from calentura in Panama). Mummy of Inca prince found in Peruvian valley four days west of Cuzco, lake, mortarless masonry, cave; lying supine, body unembalmed, perfect. Djama proposes resuscitation experiment; bargain: half of treasures.

**PROLOGUE II "A Physiological Experiment":** One week later; Djama's laboratory. Mummy revived; speaks Quichua: "Cori-Coyllur, Nustallipa, Nusta mi!" Lamson faints. Inca Vilcaroya awakes ("Am I only dreaming that the death-sleep is over?"). Asks for Golden Star (his sister-bride; both died/entombed in Sanctuary of Sun at Cuzco, 1532, after Atahuallpa's capture at Cajamarca and Huascar's murder). Djama's sister RUTH (Joyful Star, "Cusi-Coyllur") to nurse.

**CHAPTER I "Back through the Shadows":** Vilcaroya's narrative. Capt. Francis Hartness (English soldier, ~30, golden hair, blue eyes) met at Panama. Journey via Arequipa (Misti volcano), Sicuani, Cuzco.

**CHAPTER II "Brothers of the Blood":** Tupac-Rayca, great-grandson of Tupac-Amaru; San Sebastian village; Ullullo. Hacienda purchase (20,000 soles). Joyful Star shocked by sister-marriage; Hartness counsels Vilcaroya.

**CHAPTER III "In the Hall of Gold":** Vilcaroya leads Djama blindfolded to Sayacusca (Tired Stone) at Rodadero; hidden hall of gold; mummies on golden chairs; Vilcaroya dresses in Huascar's robes. Gold sold to pay hacienda.

**CHAPTER IV "The Sister Stars":** Journey to lake resting-place of Golden Star beside Umantai (twin peaks). Joyful Star and Golden Star look alike. Vilcaroya's near-love for Ruth; Hartness and Ruth attracted.

**CHAPTER V "How Djama did his Work":** Djama revives Golden Star; threatens to keep her; Vilcaroya's dagger; Djama agrees to sister-exchange.

**CHAPTER VI "The Waking of Golden Star":** Golden Star awakens with Ruth's kiss; memory blank, child-like. Hartness and Vilcaroya pact.

**CHAPTER VII "In the Throne-room of Yupanqui":** Djama proposes Golden Star to go to England; Ruth takes Golden Star. Vilcaroya shows Ruth Hall of Gold; proposes to Ruth in throne-room (Yupanqui's throne).

**CHAPTER VIII "How the Soul of Golden Star came back":** Vilcaroya presented to Children of the Blood; Hartness made war-leader; plan for revolt; hidden passages; Golden Star's first words.

**CHAPTER IX "The Treachery of Djama":** Djama betrays to Governor Don Antonio Prada (son Coronel Prada); soldiers captured in Hall of Gold; Djama and Spanish officer immured in golden cell; Djama's cell "grave of gold".

**CHAPTER X "On the Rodadero":** Ruth/Vilcaroya; Golden Star's affection for Hartness; preparations; sentry killed.

**CHAPTER XI "How we took the City of the Sun":** Battle at Sayacusca; Governor surrenders; Cuartel taken; two machine-guns; Hartness made governor of Cuzco.

**CHAPTER XII "Queen and Crown":** Ruth affirms love; Vilcaroya proclaimed Inca at sunrise, Rainbow Banner.

**CHAPTER XIII "How Djama paid his debt":** Djama shoots at Vilcaroya; Ullullo killed; Djama dies by will-stopping breath.

**CHAPTER XIV "The Re-kindling of the Sacred Fire":** Feast of Raymi; Sacred Fleece kindled; Vilcaroya and Ruth ("Joyful Star") wed by golden marriage-font (wine and water); Hartness and Golden Star also wed. Footnote: Church of Santo Domingo built over Temple of the Sun.

Key names: Vilcaroya-Inca, Golden Star (Cori-Coyllur), Joyful Star (Ruth Djama), Laurens Djama, Professor Martin Lamson, Francis Hartness, Tupac-Rayca, Ullullo, Anahuac, Ainu, Anda-Huillac, Governor Antonio Prada, Coronel Prada, Huayna-Capac, Huascar, Atahuallpa, Manco Capac, Mama Occlu, Yupanqui.
